properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 3:58AM MDT until October 12 at 7:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Mesa County in west central Colorado in and
around the Turner Gulch Burn Scar...

* WHEN...Until 700 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 356 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southwestern Mesa County near the Turner
Gulch Burn Scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 3:57AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA... Yuma, Kit Carson, Cheyenne KS and Dundy
counties.

* TIMING... 9 AM MDT to 4 PM MDT (10 AM MDT to 5 PM CDT). Duration
of strong winds and low humidities together expected to be 1 to
2 hours.

* WINDS... West southwesterly 15 to 30 mph in the morning,
decreasing through the afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY... Falling to 10 to 15 percent in the
afternoon.

* TEMPERATURES... Lower to mid 80s.

* FUELS... Fuels will promote fire spread if fires were to
develop.

* FIRE DANGER...Lowest humidities will overlap with stronger
winds for an hour or two this afternoon. While not expected to
be widespread or persistent, these conditions could make
controlling any fire difficult.

Outdoor burning and activities that cause open sparks or flames
are discouraged. Fire and emergency officials should be aware that
weather conditions will be favorable for the development of grass
and crop fires.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

A strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw
in tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this
weekend. This strong southerly fetch will draw anomalously high
moisture content across the Desert Southwest and into eastern Utah
and western Colorado. The chance for widespread precipitation
increases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts
range from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts
favoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.

Embedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing
the threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain. While
confidence in location and rainfall rates remain low at this time,
the potential for rapidly rising rivers, streams, normally dry
arroyos and slot canyons are possible Sunday through Monday.

Please follow the evolving forecast, especially if your plans
including recreating or commuting across eastern Utah and western
Colorado Sunday onward. Also, keep in mind weather potential above
your location and upstream, particularly for those who reside below
sensitive terrain like recent burn scars.
